components.name: playwright-core
components.scope: dev + optional peer (M1b browser engine; never installed automatically for consumers)
components.source: https://registry.npmjs.org/playwright-core (publisher: Microsoft, repo github.com/microsoft/playwright); published 2026-10-14, 20 days before review; zero dependencies; no install scripts

components.advisories_checked: npm audit 2026-11-03 (full tree with playwright-core): 0 vulnerabilities

services_and_tools.name: GitHub (repository hosting)
services_and_tools.usage: Git hosting of this public repository, owner-created version tags and GitHub Releases with a locally built `npm pack` tarball attached. No GitHub Actions, no Dependabot, no GitHub Apps, no automated bulk API activity.
services_and_tools.findings: Dual-use security research tooling is permitted. Prohibited: using GitHub to deliver attacks or gain unauthorized access, automated excessive bulk activity, inauthentic automated accounts, posting third-party personal information. Customer data from assessment reports must never be committed.

services_and_tools.name: Agent host plugin formats (Claude Code marketplace, Codex plugins, Gemini CLI extensions, Antigravity plugins)
services_and_tools.usage: Static manifest files in this repository (.claude-plugin/, .codex-plugin/, .agents/plugins/marketplace.json, gemini-extension.json, .antigravity-plugin/) that the user's own host reads when the user installs from this Git repository. NavSentry calls no host API, creates no account, publishes to no hosted catalog and runs no host command; `navsentry doctor` only reads local files and prints the host's own commands.
services_and_tools.findings: File formats checked 2026-10-31: Claude manifests pass `claude plugin validate --strict` (Claude Code 2.1.302); Codex manifest fields match installed Codex CLI 0.166.0 plugin examples; Antigravity schema https://antigravity.google/schemas/v1/plugin.json (additionalProperties false, version supported, .antigravity-plugin/plugin.json takes precedence in multi-provider repos). Gemini CLI and agy were not available locally, so their end-to-end installs are unverified. Submitting to an official hosted marketplace would need a separate terms review.

services_and_tools.name: GitHub Actions / Dependabot / scheduled workflows
services_and_tools.findings: Owner prohibits GitHub-hosted automation after a previous account suspension. All gates run locally via `npm run gate`.
services_and_tools.review_due: never (owner decision; change only by new explicit owner decision)

services_and_tools.name: npm public registry (install only)
services_and_tools.usage: Installing pinned dev dependencies; `npm audit` advisory lookup during the local gate. No publishing.
services_and_tools.findings: No account needed to install. Must not strain infrastructure with unreasonable request volume; must not crawl the website. Normal install/audit volume is far below limits.

services_and_tools.name: Node.js runtime
services_and_tools.findings: MIT-style license with bundled third-party notices (OpenSSL Apache-2.0, etc.). Not redistributed by NavSentry.

services_and_tools.name: Playwright browser binaries (Chromium headless shell only)
services_and_tools.usage: M1b `--engine playwright` (development profile only). The user installs the browser explicitly with `npx playwright-core install --only-shell chromium`; NavSentry never downloads it. Every page request is fulfilled by NavSentry's own direct-http transport (ScopeGate + Budget); the browser itself gets no usable network path (see docs/adr/0008-playwright-engine-s1.md).
services_and_tools.findings: Owner approved 2026-11-03. Default browsers are open-source Chromium builds downloaded from Microsoft's CDN (host overridable with PLAYWRIGHT_DOWNLOAD_HOST); Chromium is BSD-3-Clause-style licensed. The browsers page states no separate EULA or CDN terms for these downloads. Branded `chrome`/`msedge` channels fall under Google/Microsoft terms and are NOT approved; Firefox and WebKit builds are not reviewed and NOT approved. NavSentry does not redistribute browser binaries; NOTICE attribution applies only if NavSentry ever bundles Playwright code. The install command also fetched Playwright's helper builds ffmpeg (shipped with COPYING.LGPLv2.1; used by Playwright only for video recording, which NavSentry never enables) and winldd (Windows dependency check). They are not redistributed by NavSentry.

services_and_tools.name: Playwright Chromium full build (headed visual driver)
services_and_tools.usage: SPEC-0.3.0 §5 / owner decision D6: `navsentry browse start --headed` would show NavSentry's own browser in a visible window. The user would install it explicitly with `npx playwright-core install chromium`; NavSentry would never download it. The network path is the same as the headless shell (every request fulfilled through direct-http, ScopeGate and the Budget).
services_and_tools.findings: Not yet reviewed. Same open-source Chromium source and download host as the approved headless shell, but a different, larger binary with a GUI. Until an owner review records APPROVED, the code refuses --headed (HEADED_BROWSER_APPROVED = false in src/transports/playwright.ts). Branded chrome/msedge channels stay NOT approved.

services_and_tools.name: curl / PowerShell (optional OS executables)
services_and_tools.usage: Detected from fixed system paths only; execution adapters scheduled for M3.
services_and_tools.findings: curl license (MIT-like); PowerShell 7 MIT; Windows PowerShell 5.1 is part of Windows (OS license). Not redistributed.

services_and_tools.name: OWASP Top 10 / WSTG / ASVS (reference content)
services_and_tools.usage: Category IDs and names only, for mapping. No OWASP text copied.
services_and_tools.findings: OWASP projects are generally CC BY-SA 4.0. Using identifiers/names with links is attribution-compatible. Top 10:2025 and ASVS 5.0.0 (30 May 2025) verified as current on 2026-10-31.

services_and_tools.name: SaaS advisory APIs (OSV, NVD, GitHub Advisory API), Postman cloud, OWASP ZAP
services_and_tools.findings: Each requires its own terms review (rate limits, API keys, data sharing of target information, acceptable use) before any integration. Target data must never be sent to a SaaS without the target owner's approval.

services_and_tools.name: GitHub Advisory Database (advisory source for the knowledge base)
services_and_tools.usage: Primary source for real records in src/knowledge/advisories.ts. A maintainer reads individual reviewed advisories (github.com/advisories/GHSA-… pages or the matching OSV-format file in github/advisory-database) and copies only facts (IDs, package, affected/fixed ranges, severity, dates, URL) after verification. No GitHub API, no scheduled or bulk automated download, no scan-time network access (S12).
services_and_tools.findings: Owner approved 2026-11-03. Data is CC-BY 4.0: attribution to the GitHub Advisory Database with a link to each advisory is required and is carried in every record's source URL and in the generated KB header. Manual per-record reading stays far below any automated-use concern in the GitHub AUP. OSV.dev was considered and NOT adopted: its FAQ and site state no data license or terms of use (missing evidence = blocked).

services_and_tools.name: Visual driver: screenshots handed to the host agent (and its model provider)
services_and_tools.usage: `navsentry browse` writes PNG screenshots of the target into the run's work directory; the host agent reads them. NavSentry itself calls no model or visual provider API and sends nothing off the machine.
services_and_tools.findings: Owner approved 2026-11-04 (ADR-0009). The data flow to a provider is the host agent's, under the host's own terms; NavSentry's condition is per-target owner consent through manifest `transports.visual_computer_use: true`, development profile only. Integrating a provider API directly would need its own terms review and is NOT adopted.

services_and_tools.name: Chrome Web Store and Microsoft Edge Add-ons (distribution of the NavSentry Recorder extension)
services_and_tools.usage: Not used. SPEC-0.3.0 owner decision D7: the recorder is distributed unpacked from the repository and releases only.
services_and_tools.findings: Publishing would bind the project to each store's developer agreement and program policies and needs a developer account. Not reviewed; review before any store listing.
